en.title: Minimum Operations to Zero an Array with Prefix Plus or Minus One
en.description:
One operation chooses a non-empty prefix and applies +1 or −1 to all of its elements simultaneously. Find the minimum number of operations to make every element zero. These are not suffix operations.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the integers. 1≤n≤100000, −10^9≤element≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 5 and 1. In the second example the absolute value of the first element cannot be used in place of the last.
hints: The answer is the absolute value of the last element plus the absolute value of every adjacent difference.
